description: Set parameters for a groundwater fluid flow analysis. Settings include biot, cmodel, anisotropic, isotropic, null, fastflow, fastflow-relaxation, implicit, property, saturation-tolerance, time-total, track, zone-based-pp, group, tail, tortuosity, pressure-cutoff.

keywords.name: biot
keywords.description: The fluid-flow calculation uses the Biot coefficient, \(α\), and the Biot modulus, \(M\), if on. If off, then the fluid modulus, \(K_f\), and porosity, \(n\), are used and \(α\) = 1. The default is off. See Biot Coefficient and Biot Modulus.

keywords.name: cmodel
keywords.description: Associates a fluid constitutive model with specified zones in the grid. It also allows querying of properties and states of constitutive models. Options: assign {anisotropic | isotropic | null} [range]: assigns a fluid model to all zones in the range . This keyword may only be given if the model is configured for fluid calculations (see model configure fluid ). Fluid models are described in Grid Configured for Fluid Flow . Options: anisotropic: Assign the anisotropic flow model.; isotropic: Assign the isotropic flow model.; null: Assign the null fluid model.; list: List the available fluid constitutive models and their properties.

keywords.description: Assign the anisotropic flow model.

keywords.name: cmodel-assign-isotropic
keywords.description: Assign the isotropic flow model.

keywords.name: cmodel-assign-null
keywords.description: Assign the null fluid model.

keywords.name: cmodel-list
keywords.description: List the available fluid constitutive models and their properties.

keywords.name: fastflow
keywords.description: Turns the fastflow solution scheme on and off. See Fully Saturated Fast Flow.

keywords.name: fastflow-relaxation
keywords.description: Sets the relaxation parameters used in the fastflow solution scheme.

keywords.name: implicit
keywords.description: The implicit solution scheme in the fluid flow model is turned on or off. The default is off.

keywords.name: saturation-tolerance
keywords.description: The effect of saturation changes to gridpoints is only applied when the accumulated saturation change is greater than this value. This is done for efficiency of calculation. The default value is 1x10:exp:\(-3\)

keywords.name: time-total
keywords.description: Specifies the accumulated zone fluid time, defined as the sum of all the timesteps over which zone fluid is active. Once set, fluid time will continue to accumulate with subsequent cycles.

keywords.name: track
keywords.syntax: track {active <b> | create {point <v>... [[zonefluidblock]] | line {begin <v> | end <v> | segment <i>} ... [[zonefluidblock]] | plane {begin <v> | end-1 <v> | end-2 <v> | segment <i1> <i2>} ... [[zonefluidblock]]} | delete [range] | group <s> {remove | slot <s>} [range] | list [path] | trace [name <s>] <i>}
keywords.description: Options: active <b>: Turns particle tracking on or off . track is off by default.; create {point <v>... [[zonefluidblock]] | line {begin <v> | end <v> | segment <i>} ... [[zonefluidblock]] | plane {begin <v> | end-1 <v> | end-2 <v> | segment <i1><i2>} ... [[zonefluidblock]]}: Create one or more particles in zones. The location and number of the particles created are controlled by the following keywords. The <[zonefluidblock]> following can be used to specify attributes on the created particles. Options: point <v>... [[zonefluidblock]]: Place a particle in the grid at the specified location v . For each vector value given, another particle will be created.; line {begin <v> | end <v> | segment <i>} ... [[zonefluidblock]]: Add particles to the grid along a line. Options: begin <v>: Specify the start position of the line. The default value is (0,0,0).; end <v>: Specify the end position of the line. The default value is (0,0,0).; segment <i>: Specify the line be divided equally into i + 1 segments, causing i particles to be introduced into the grid. The default value is 2.; plane {begin <v> | end-1 <v> | end-2 <v> | segment <i1><i2>} ... [[zonefluidblock]]: Add particles to the grid along a plane defined by two lines. Options: begin <v>: Specifies the shared start point of both lines that will define the plane. The default value is (0,0,0).; end-1 <v>: Specifies end of the first line. The default value is (0,0,0).; end-2 <v>: Specifies end of the second line. The default value is (0,0,0).; segment <i1><i2>: Divides the first line into i1 + 1 equal segments; divides the second line into i2 + 1 equal segments. i1 x i2 particles will be introduced to the grid on an evenly spaced grid along the plane. The default value of i1 and i2 is 2.; delete [range]: Delete particles within the given range .; group <s>{remove | slot <s>} [range]: Assign or remove groups to particles in the range. Use of the group logic is described in Groups . Options: remove: Remove the group s from particles within the given range. This does not remove the particles themselves.; slot <s>: Assign groups in the given range to the slot named s . By default groups will be assigned to slot Default; list [path]: lists summary information about tracking particles. If the path keyword is omitted, the current particle position information is output. If the path keyword is included, then particle path information is output.; trace [name <s>] <i>: Creates a location trace (see the trace command) of the particle with ID number i .

keywords.name: zone-based-pp
keywords.description: Specify that pore-pressures should be retrieved directly from the zone, rather than averaged from the gridpoints. Zone pore pressures must be assigned manually via FISH, using the zone.pp intrinsic.

keywords.name: group
keywords.description: Assign the created particles to the group s1 and (if supplied) assign that group to slot s2. By default the slot name will be Default.

keywords.name: tail
keywords.description: When on (the default setting), particles will automatically store a list of coordinates along their path as they move through the grid. If off particles will only keep track of their current position.

keywords.name: tortuosity
keywords.description: The tortuosity is specified as f, which is defined as the ratio of the straight line path to the actual fluid path through a zone. This factor will be used to multiply track increments calculated from the flow velocity; it defaults to 1 if not given.

keywords.name: active
keywords.description: Turn the fluid module computations on or off. Active by default once the fluid process is configured.

keywords.name: biot
keywords.description: Turn biot mode on or off. When on, fluid pore-pressure changes are computed using the Biot effective stress formulation.

keywords.name: fastflow
keywords.description: Turn the fastflow solution scheme on or off. Fastflow is an accelerated time-stepping scheme suitable when pore-pressure changes are quasi-static.

keywords.name: fastflow-relaxation
keywords.description: Set the relaxation parameter used in the fastflow solution scheme. Default 0.004.

keywords.name: implicit
keywords.description: Turn implicit mode on or off. When on, the fluid solver advances pore-pressure using an implicit timestep (which must be set manually); when off, the solver uses the explicit local-flow timestep. Default off. Options: solver-jacobi: Use the iterative Jacobi solver based on the local matrix formulation (see Implicit Formulation ). Note that specifying a timestep that is too large can cause the Jacobi solver to fail to converge. If this keyword is specified and the solver diverges, the system will exit with an error message. The benefit of using the Jacobi solver compared to other solvers is that it is usually faster for small implicit timesteps (<< the divergence timestep).; solver-direct [{preserve}]: Use the direct solver similar to matrix inversion (see Advanced implicit solvers ). This highly efficient solver is able to handle small to medium size models (< 50-100K zones) and it is unconditionally stable for any timestep. Before this solver is called, the global right-hand-side (RHS) vector and global coefficient matrix (M) are formed for the whole model to incorporate contributions from all relevant gridpoints. Then the solver solves a system of linear equations for unknown global vector of pore pressure changes. The following keyword is available: Options: preserve: Specify to preserve the global pressure coefficients matrix and only update its diagonal containing timestep-dependent terms. In general, the global matrix M must be re-created each time the implicit solver is called as model parameters, such as geometry, physical properties, implicit timestep, etc., may change. However, if the model parameters do not change during the simulation but user wishes to specify a different implicit timestep (e.g., to gradually increase it every certain number of steps), only the diagonal terms of the global matrix must be updated, which is very efficient. To stop this procedure and form a new global pressure coefficients matrix, the command zone thermal implicit must be issued (this resets the implicit solvers settings).; solver-pcg [{tolerance | iterations-limit {preserve}}]: Use the preconditioned conjugate gradient iterative solver (see Advanced implicit solvers ). This highly efficient solver is able to handle very large models and it is unconditionally stable for any timestep due to its special technique of matching desired solution accuracy to the number of iterations required to reach this accuracy. Before the solver is called, the global right-hand-side (RHS) vector and global pressure coefficients matrix (M) are created for the whole model to incorporate contributions from all relevant gridpoints. Then the solver analyses matrix properties (eigenvalues, condition number) and determines the required number of iterations, after which the iterative solution procedure starts. The following keywords are available. Options: tolerance: Specify an error tolerance (solution accuracy) that will determine when to stop iterations. The default tolerance value is 1.e-6.; iterations-limit {preserve}: Specify the limit on the number of iterations. By default, the number of iterations is determined based on the analysis of the global matrix properties, such as minimum/maximum eigenvalues and the the condition number. This analysis is usually done rather fast, and it assures that the system can be solved to reach desired solution accuracy. Specifying a limit on the number of iteration skips the global matrix analysis, which may decrease overall solution time, but the risk of this is that the number of iterations specified may be insufficient to reach desired accuracy. The pcg solver has a general limit of 1000 on the number of iterations. Options: preserve: Specify to preserve the global pressure coefficients matrix and only update its diagonal containing timestep-dependent terms. For detailed description see the equivalent usage above with the solver-direct keyword.

keywords.name: pressure-cutoff
keywords.description: Turn the pore-pressure cutoff (Pcut) mode on or off. When on, negative pore pressures are clamped at zero (a useful approximation in unsaturated regions).

keywords.name: saturation-tolerance
keywords.description: Set the saturation convergence tolerance used by the fluid solver. Default 1e-3.

keywords.name: time-total
keywords.description: Set the total accumulated fluid-flow time.

keywords.name: zone-based-pp
keywords.description: When on, pore pressures are retrieved directly from the zone (which must have been assigned manually via FISH using zone.pp) rather than averaged from the gridpoints.

keywords.description: Assign, query, or list the fluid constitutive model for zones in the range. Sub-keywords: assign, list, plus the three model name shortcuts (anisotropic, isotropic, null).

keywords.description: Assign the named fluid constitutive model to all zones in the range. Sub-keywords are anisotropic, isotropic, and null.

keywords.description: Assign the anisotropic fluid model (permeabilities can be given along three principal directions or as a 3x3 tensor).

keywords.name: cmodel-assign-isotropic
keywords.description: Assign the isotropic fluid model (single hydraulic-conductivity / permeability scalar).

keywords.name: cmodel-assign-null
keywords.description: Assign the null fluid model (no fluid flow in the zone).

keywords.name: cmodel-list
keywords.description: List the available fluid constitutive models and their property names.

keywords.description: List current FluidModule settings (configured/active state, accumulated time, implicit/biot/pcut/fastflow flags, saturation tolerance, fastflow relaxation coefficient). Options: information: Output current configuration settings and status information for the fluid model.; property {biot <f> | hydraulic-conductivity <f> | porosity <f> | undrained-thermal-coefficient <f> | permeability <f> | dip <f>3D Only | dip-direction <f>3D Only | permeability-1 <f> | permeability-2 <f> | permeability-3 <f>3D Only | permeability-xx <f> | permeability-xy <f> | permeability-xz <f>3D Only | permeability-yy <f> | permeability-yz <f>3D Only | permeability-zz <f>3D Only | rotation <f>} [range]: Output the values of the specified fluid property in all zones in the range. Only one between hydraulic conductivity and permeability is needed.; dip <f>3D Only: List the principal permeability plane dip angle (in degrees).; dip-direction <f>3D Only: List the principal permeability plane dip direction angle (in degrees).; permeability-1 <f>: List the principal permeability value.; permeability-2 <f>: List the principal permeability value.; permeability-3 <f>3D Only: List the principal permeability value.; permeability-xx <f>: List the xx -component of permeability.; permeability-xy <f>: List the xy -component of permeability.; permeability-xz <f>3D Only: List the xz -component of permeability.; permeability-yy <f>: List the yy -component of permeability.; permeability-yz <f>3D Only: List the yz -component of permeability.; permeability-zz <f>3D Only: List the zz -component of permeability.; rotation <f>: List the principal permeability plane rotation angle (in degrees).

keywords.name: property
keywords.description: Set a fluid material property. The property name must match a property of the currently-assigned fluid constitutive model (isotropic: hydraulic-conductivity, porosity, biot, permeability, undrained-thermal-coefficient; anisotropic adds dip, dip-direction, hydraulic-conductivity-{1,2,3,xx,xy,xz,yy,yz,zz}, permeability-{1,2,3,xx,xy,xz,yy,yz,zz}, rotation). Options: biot <f>: Set the biot coefficient (grain compressibility), \(\alpha\) . The default is 1.0.; porosity <f>: Set porosity, \(n\) . The default is 0.5.; undrained-thermal-coefficient <f>: Set the undrained thermal coefficient, \(\beta\) .; hydraulic-conductivity <f>: Set isotropic hydraulic conductivity (units of length/time). Gravity and water density must be defined to use this quanitity. Only one of hydraulic-conductivity or permeability needs to be assigned.; permeability <f>: Set isotropic permeability, \(k\) . The permeability used in FLAC is defined as the conventional hydraulic permeability divided by the unit weight of water. Permeability must be non-zero if the command zone fluid active on applies. Only one of hydraulic-conductivity or permeability needs to be assigned.; dip <f>3D Only: Set the principal permeability plane dip angle (in degrees).; dip-direction <f>3D Only: Set the principal permeability plane dip direction angle (in degrees).; hydraulic-conductivity-1 <f>: Set the principal hydraulic conductivity value (units of length/time).; hydraulic-conductivity-2 <f>: Set the principal hydraulic conductivity value (units of length/time).; hydraulic-conductivity-3 <f>3D only: Set the principal hydraulic conductivity value (units of length/time).; hydraulic-conductivity-xx <f>: Set the xx -component of hydraulic conductivity (units of length/time).; hydraulic-conductivity-xy <f>: Set the xy -component of hydraulic conductivity (units of length/time).; hydraulic-conductivity-xz <f>3D only: Set the xz -component of hydraulic conductivity (units of length/time).; hydraulic-conductivity-yy <f>: Set the yy -component of hydraulic conductivity (units of length/time).; hydraulic-conductivity-yz <f>3D only: Set the yz -component of hydraulic conductivity (units of length/time).; hydraulic-conductivity-zz <f>3D only: Set the zz -component of hydraulic conductivity (units of length/time).; permeability-1 <f>: Set the principal permeability value.; permeability-2 <f>: Set the principal permeability value.; permeability-3 <f>3D Only: Set the principal permeability value.; permeability-xx <f>: Set the xx -component of permeability.; permeability-xy <f>: Set the xy -component of permeability.; permeability-xz <f>3D Only: Set the xz -component of permeability.; permeability-yy <f>: Set the yy -component of permeability.; permeability-yz <f>3D Only: Set the yz -component of permeability.; permeability-zz <f>3D Only: Set the zz -component of permeability.; rotation <f>: Set the principal permeability plane rotation angle (in degrees).

keywords.name: property-distributed
keywords.description: Set a fluid material property with an optional spatial distribution. Same property names as property; the optional distribution-block sub-keyword controls how the base value is varied: add, deviation-gaussian, deviation-uniform, gradient, multiply, vary.

keywords.name: property-distributed-add
keywords.description: Add the supplied value to the existing property value in each zone.

keywords.name: property-distributed-deviation-gaussian
keywords.description: Apply Gaussian-distributed deviation around the base value with standard deviation f.

keywords.name: property-distributed-deviation-uniform
keywords.description: Apply uniformly-distributed deviation around the base value with half-width f.

keywords.name: property-distributed-gradient
keywords.description: Apply a linear gradient v to the property value (optionally referenced to the supplied origin).

keywords.name: property-distributed-multiply
keywords.description: Multiply the existing property value in each zone by the supplied value.

keywords.name: property-distributed-vary
keywords.description: Apply a linear variation v to the property value across the range.

keywords.description: End of the line for track create line.

keywords.name: track-create-line-segment
keywords.description: Number of segments along the line (i+1 particles will be created).

keywords.name: track-create-plane
keywords.description: Create (i1+1)*(i2+1) particles on a planar grid spanned by the begin point and the two end vectors.

keywords.name: track-create-plane-begin
keywords.description: Origin corner of the plane.

keywords.name: track-create-plane-end-1
keywords.description: First edge endpoint of the plane (from begin to end-1).

keywords.name: track-create-plane-end-2
keywords.description: Second edge endpoint of the plane (from begin to end-2).

keywords.name: track-create-plane-segment
keywords.description: Number of segments along the first and second plane edges.

keywords.name: track-delete
keywords.description: Delete particles in the range (or all particles if no range supplied).

keywords.name: track-group
keywords.description: Assign group s to particles in the range. Optional slot s places the group in the named slot (default slot name is Default). remove unassigns the group instead.

keywords.name: track-group-slot
keywords.description: Slot the group is assigned to (default 'Default').

keywords.name: track-group-remove
keywords.description: Remove the named group from particles in the range.

keywords.name: track-list
keywords.description: List all currently-tracked particles, their coordinates, tortuosity, containing zone, accumulated path length, and status.

keywords.name: track-trace
keywords.description: Add a named trace of an individual particle (by id i) so its path can be queried later via the FISH trace API.
